rules.title: Types are interned by canonical structural identity
rules.statement: Every type has a canonical identity: two types constructed structurally identically (per the per-kind identity fields below, computed bottom-up over already-canonical sub-types) denote the same type and intern to one shared representative; structurally distinct types intern to distinct representatives.

rules.title: Lifetimes excluded from type identity for & / &mut
rules.statement: Reference types `&'a T` and `&mut 'a T` have identity determined solely by mutability and pointee `T`; the lifetime `'a` is NOT part of type identity (matches types_equal). Lifetime args on struct/enum/assoc types likewise do not affect type equality.
rules.divergence: Rust treats lifetimes as part of the type but as a separate region-check phase; identity-collapse of lifetimes here matches Rust's type-equality-modulo-regions.

rules.title: Raw pointer identity = (mutability, pointee, zoned-flag)
rules.statement: Raw pointer `*const T`, `*mut T`, and `*zoned T` are mutually distinct types: identity = (mut flag, zoned flag carried in const_val bit 0, pointee T). `*zoned T` interns distinctly from a plain `*T`.

rules.title: Array identity includes the length
rules.statement: Array `[T; N]` identity = (length N, symbolic-length variable name, element T). Arrays with different lengths (concrete or symbolic) are distinct types.

rules.title: Struct/enum identity = (package, name, type-args)
rules.statement: A nominal struct or enum type's identity = (package name, type/enum name, ordered type arguments). Two instantiations of a generic nominal type with different type arguments are distinct types; zoned structs share this scheme.

rules.title: Tuple identity = ordered element types
rules.statement: A tuple type's identity is the ordered sequence of its element types; tuples are equal iff same arity and pairwise-equal elements.

rules.title: Slice identity = (mutability, owning kind, element)
rules.statement: Slice types are distinguished by element T, mutability, and owning kind (const_val): `&[T]`, `&mut [T]`, and owning `Box<[T]>` are mutually distinct types.
rules.divergence: A3 (custom-DST / Box<[T]> as owning slice kind)

rules.title: Trait-object identity = (owning kind, auto-traits, trait, type-args)
rules.statement: A trait-object `dyn Trait<..>` identity = (owning kind {Borrow/Box/Rc/Arc} in const_val low byte, `+Send` bit 8, `+Sync` bit 9, trait name, trait type-args). `&dyn T` and `&dyn T + Send` are distinct types; the same trait behind Box vs Rc vs Arc are distinct.

rules.title: Custom-DST reference identity = (package, name, mutability, owning kind, type-args)
rules.statement: A custom-DST reference type's identity = (package, struct name, mutability, owning kind {Borrow/Box}, type-args); an owning `Box<Foo>` custom-DST is distinct from a borrowed `&Foo`.

rules.title: Function-pointer identity = (ABI tag, params, return)
rules.statement: A function-pointer type identity = (extern-ABI tag where empty = default Rust ABI, ordered parameter types, return type). Function pointers differing only in ABI are distinct types.

rules.title: Each function item is a distinct zero-sized type
rules.statement: A function-item type's identity = (function symbol name, turbofish type-args, signature params, return). Two distinct functions with identical signatures get distinct fn-item types, and distinct instantiations of one generic function (even when the resulting fn-ptr signature collapses, e.g. unused type param) get distinct fn-item types.

rules.title: Associated-type identity = (trait, assoc name, base, GAT args)
rules.statement: An associated/projection type identity = (trait name, associated-type name, base type, generic-associated-type arguments). GATs differing in their args are distinct projection types.

rules.title: Integer-literal placeholder identity carries its value
rules.statement: An inferred integer-literal type `{integer}` carrying a const value is identified by that value (const_val); two literal placeholders with different values do not collapse to one type.

rules.title: WritStatic-literal type identity = its byte-hash
rules.statement: A type parameterized by a WritStatic literal config (`Foo::<@{...}>`) is identified by the byte-hash of that literal; distinct configurations instantiate to distinct types and do not dedupe.

rules.title: Config-slot type identity = (cfg-typevar name, slot key)
rules.statement: A config-slot type is identified by the pair (config type-variable name, slot key); distinct slots intern to distinct types.

rules.title: Type/const variable identity = name
rules.statement: A type variable or const variable is identified by its name (plus const_val); two type parameters with the same name denote the same type variable.

rules.title: Primitive types identified by kind alone
rules.statement: Primitive types carry no structural fields; their kind tag alone identifies them, so all occurrences of a given primitive are the same interned type.

rules.title: Post-interning, type equality = pointer/UID equality
rules.statement: After interning, every type has a unique representative, so type equality reduces to representative-identity: equal hash/UID implies type-equal, and identical reference trivially implies type-equal (lifetime, package, lifetime-args, const_val being the only fields that may share a hash bucket while differing).
